problem: What is the parametrization of the curve $r(t)=⟨t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,3,\,t\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,$ $t\ge 0,$ by its arc length $s?$
worked_solution:
First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨t\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,0,\,-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(t\operatorname{cos}⁡t)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{(-t\operatorname{sin}⁡t)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡t+{t}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}} \\  & =|t| \\  & =t\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the arc length of the curve from $0$ to $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}s & ={\int }_{0}^{t}‖{r}^{′}(u)‖\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{u}^{2}\,{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & =\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $s=\frac{{t}^{2}}{2},$ we have that $t=\sqrt{2s}.$

Therefore, the vector function that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\sqrt{2s}) \\  & =⟨\sqrt{2s}\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{2s}+\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{2s},\,3,\,\sqrt{2s}\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{2s}-\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{2s}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
